title: Stacks and queues
syllabusDesc: Add/remove from one end (stack) or opposite ends (queue).
inlineSample:
stack = []
stack.append("first")
stack.append("second")
print(stack.pop())  # second

from collections import deque
q = deque(["a", "b"])
q.append("c")
print(q.popleft())  # a
desc: Stacks are LIFO (last-in, first-out), great for undo, parsing, and DFS. Queues are FIFO (first-in, first-out), great for scheduling and BFS.
placeholder:
# Build a tiny stack and queue
stack = []
queue = []

# your code here
solution:
stack = []
stack.append("nav-home")
stack.append("nav-profile")
print("stack pop:", stack.pop())  # remove last
print("stack now:", stack)

from collections import deque
queue = deque()
queue.append("task1")
queue.append("task2")
queue.appendleft("urgent")
print("queue pop left:", queue.popleft())
print("queue now:", list(queue))
techniques: Use list append/pop for stack operations
Use collections.deque for O(1) queue operations at both ends
Map real problems (undo, BFS) to stack/queue choices
challenges: Check for balanced parentheses with a stack
Simulate printer jobs with a queue
Implement a browser back/forward history with two stacks
notes:
list.pop(0) is O(n); use deque for fast left pops/appends.

Keep APIs small: push/pop for stacks, enqueue/dequeue for queues.
